facts.claim: An overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised in Australia.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller (DFAT), Getting married overseas
facts.use_note: Legal. Page last updated 18/08/2026. Use for the FAQ 'Can an Italian wedding planner make our marriage legal in Australia?'. Add that requirements must be confirmed for your own passports and that the Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: For an overseas marriage to be recognised in Australia it must have been valid under the law of the country where it happened and valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller (DFAT), Getting married overseas
facts.use_note: Legal. Explains why a symbolic ceremony alone does not create a legal marriage: legality comes from the Italian civil (or recognised religious) process, not from the planner.

facts.claim: A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted in Australia as proof of marriage but may not be usable as proof of a name change; Smartraveller advises checking with your state registry of births, deaths and marriages and talking to a lawyer to confirm the certificate is valid in Australia.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller (DFAT), Getting married overseas
facts.use_note: Legal. Good for the paying-parent reader. Do not turn into legal advice; point to the legal guide.

facts.claim: Australian citizens marrying in Italy need a Nulla Osta presented to the Italian City Council where the wedding takes place. To get it, each Australian first signs an Atto Notorio with four witnesses, declaring there is no impediment to the marriage. In Australia the Atto Notorio is issued by the Italian Consulate General for your state of residence (Sydney covers NSW); in Italy, by any Tribunal.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia Sydney (Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs), Atto Notorio
facts.use_note: Legal. Keep to one or two sentences and link the Italy legal guide. Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth readers use their own state's consulate.

facts.claim: At the Sydney consulate the couple and all four witnesses must attend the appointment in person; witnesses must not be related to the bride or groom (they may be related to each other), and if both partners are Australian each signs their own Atto Notorio (the same witnesses can be used).
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia Sydney, Atto Notorio
facts.use_note: Legal. Shows the couple, not the planner, must do some steps in person in Australia. Useful for the 'what the planner handles' point.

facts.claim: The Atto Notorio is valid for six months from the date it is signed, so it cannot be issued more than six months before the wedding. The Italian City Council also needs an original birth certificate and a Single Status Certificate, each with an official Italian translation (NAATI) and an Apostille from DFAT.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia Sydney, Atto Notorio
facts.use_note: Legal. Timing matters for couples booking 12 to 18 months out: paperwork happens in the final six months. Fees: consulate refers to its consular fees page (not quoted here).

facts.claim: The Nulla Osta is a sworn declaration that must be signed in person, in Italy, before an Australian consular officer at the Australian Embassy in Rome or the Australian Consulate-General in Milan, by appointment and with an Australian passport. Nulla Ostas sworn outside Italy and Certificates of No Impediment are not valid for use in Italy.
facts.source_name: Australian Embassy Rome (DFAT), Marriage in Italy (PDF)
facts.use_note: Legal. PDF is undated and the Embassy HTML page (italy.embassy.gov.au/rome/Marriage.html) returned a server error on 23 Oct 2026, so it could not be checked against the live HTML. Consistent with the Sydney consulate page (F-04). Practical point for the article: build a Rome or Milan appointment into the couple's travel before the wedding. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Australian government representatives cannot perform marriage ceremonies, and it is not possible to get married at an Australian Embassy or Consulate.
facts.source_name: Australian Embassy Rome (DFAT), Marriage in Italy (PDF)
facts.use_note: Legal. Optional context line.

facts.claim: For a civil ceremony the couple takes the Atto Notorio and Nulla Osta to the marriage office (Ufficio Matrimoni) of the town where they will marry, lodges a Declaration of Intent to Marry and then holds the civil ceremony; the two appointments may fall on the same day. A fee for hiring the marriage hall is customary and varies by town. The Embassy advises asking the Prefettura to add an Apostille to the Italian marriage certificate so it can be used in Australia.
facts.source_name: Australian Embassy Rome (DFAT), Marriage in Italy (PDF)
facts.use_note: Legal. This is the paperwork a planner typically coordinates with the town hall; ask whether they do. Do not state a hall-hire fee.

facts.claim: The Australian Embassy in Rome notes that in the peak marriage season (May to September) it can be difficult to get an appointment with the marriage celebrant and to apply for the Apostille.
facts.source_name: Australian Embassy Rome (DFAT), Marriage in Italy (PDF)
facts.use_note: Supports asking a planner how they secure town-hall dates in peak season. No availability guarantees.

facts.claim: NSW daylight saving for 2026 to 2027 started on Sunday 4 October 2026 and ends at 3am AEDT on Sunday 4 April 2027. NSW, Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania and the ACT observe daylight saving; Queensland, Western Australia and the Northern Territory do not.
facts.source_name: NSW Government, Daylight saving
facts.use_note: Input to the Sydney and Italy time difference (F-13).

facts.claim: Across the EU, including Italy, summer time begins at 1.00 am GMT on the last Sunday in March and ends at 1.00 am GMT on the last Sunday in October.
facts.source_name: EUR-Lex, Directive 2000/84/EC on summer-time arrangements (in force)
facts.use_note: Input to F-13. Directive status shown as 'In force' on 23 Oct 2026.

facts.claim: Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST) is UTC+10; NSW, the ACT, Victoria and Tasmania move to Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT), UTC+11, from 2am on the first Sunday in October to 3am on the first Sunday in April. Queensland does not observe daylight saving.
facts.source_name: Tourism Australia, Australian time zones
facts.use_note: Input to the time difference (F-14). Dates match the NSW Government page (F-11).

facts.claim: Sydney is 8, 9 or 10 hours ahead of Italy depending on the time of year: 8 hours from early April to early October (AEST vs Italian summer time), 9 hours in the short overlaps from the first Sunday in October to the last Sunday in October and from the last Sunday in March to the first Sunday in April, and 10 hours from late October to late March (AEDT vs Italian standard time). In practice a 7pm call in Sydney is 9am to 11am in Italy, and a 5pm to 6pm call in Italy is the next morning in Sydney.
facts.source_name: Derived from Tourism Australia (F-13), NSW Government (F-11) and EU Directive 2000/84/EC (F-12); Italy's offsets (UTC+1 standard, UTC+2 summer) per F-15
facts.use_note: Calculation by research lead, not a quote. Perth is 2 hours behind Sydney in AEST months and 3 hours in AEDT months; Brisbane is the same as Sydney only from April to October. Use for the 'planning from Australia' section: a fixed weekly call slot (Sydney evening, Italy morning) is realistic.

facts.claim: Italy uses Central European Time across the whole country: UTC+1 in standard time and UTC+2 in daylight saving time.
facts.source_name: Italia.it (official Italian tourism portal), Time zones and public holidays in Italy
facts.use_note: Input to F-14. Switch dates come from the EU Directive (F-12), not this page.

facts.claim: Italy's Law 4/2013 governs 'professions not organised in orders or colleges' (professions without a statutory register or albo). It states that exercising such a profession is free, and it may be carried on individually, in partnership, as a company, a cooperative or as an employee.
facts.source_name: Gazzetta Ufficiale della Repubblica Italiana, Legge 14 gennaio 2013, n. 4 (in force 10 Feb 2013)
facts.use_note: The law does not name wedding planners. That wedding planning sits under this framework is stated by the Italian standards body's partner association context (F-18) and is consistent with there being no licence or register to look up. Writer may say: 'Italy has no licence or public register for wedding planners, so you check the business (VAT number, contract, insurance) rather than a licence number.' Do not say planners are 'unregulated' in a pejorative way.

facts.claim: Under Law 4/2013, anyone practising one of these professions must cite the law (Legge 14 gennaio 2013, n. 4) in every document and written communication with the client; failure to do so counts as an unfair commercial practice under the Italian Consumer Code.
facts.source_name: Gazzetta Ufficiale, Legge 4/2013, art. 1, comma 3
facts.use_note: Applies to planners working as individual professionals under this law; a planner trading as a company (e.g. an srl or a travel business) may operate under other rules. Use only as an optional 'detail you might spot on a contract', never as a test that a planner fails.

facts.claim: UNI, Italy's national standards body, published two standards in 2024: UNI 11954 (requirements for wedding planning and destination wedding planning services, for national and international weddings) and UNI 11955 (knowledge, skills, autonomy and responsibility requirements for wedding planners and destination wedding planners). They replace UNI/PdR 61 of 2019 and were developed with the Associazione Italiana Wedding Planner (AIWP), AIOM and Confcommercio.
facts.source_name: UNI Ente Italiano di Normazione, 'Wedding Planning di qualità: ora ci sono le norme UNI'
facts.use_note: Gives the reader a concrete question: 'Do you work to, or are you certified against, UNI 11954 or 11955?' A yes is a plus, a no is not a red flag (see F-19).

facts.claim: UNI describes its standards as voluntary technical standards (norme tecniche volontarie).
facts.source_name: UNI Ente Italiano di Normazione, home page
facts.use_note: Conflict note: an Italian planner association page (associazioneitalianaweddingplanner.it) is titled 'Le Norme UNI 11954 e 11955 sono legge'. UNI's own description (voluntary) prevails. Do not tell readers certification is mandatory.

facts.claim: Italy's Revenue Agency (Agenzia delle Entrate) offers a free online service to check whether an Italian VAT number (partita IVA) is valid and whether it is active, suspended or ceased, along with the registered business or owner name. For cross-border EU checks it points to the European Commission's VIES service.
facts.source_name: Agenzia delle Entrate, Verifica partita Iva
facts.use_note: Practical vetting step for the questions section: ask for the planner's partita IVA and full business name, then check it matches the contract and invoices. VIES: https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/. Approved-domain status of agenziaentrate.gov.it and europa.eu not in domains.md; they are government sites, flag for SEO reviewer.

facts.claim: UNI reports that Italy hosted about 12,000 destination weddings by foreign couples in 2023, worth about EUR 800 million; average spend was about EUR 50,000 per foreign wedding against about EUR 28,000 for an Italian one. Tuscany drew 35% of destination weddings, followed by Lombardy and Campania; the UK and US were the leading source markets.
facts.source_name: UNI Ente Italiano di Normazione (news article, Nov 2024)
facts.use_note: UNI does not name the underlying research. Use at most one figure, for context (e.g. 'Italy hosts around 12,000 destination weddings a year, which is why the best planners book out'). Average spend is a cost figure: see prices, Nic sign-off. Lombardy includes Lake Como; Campania includes the Amalfi Coast.

facts.claim: In Italy a SIAE licence is required to play SIAE-protected music (live or recorded) at a wedding held anywhere other than your own home, whether the ceremony is civil or religious. The licence is requested by the organiser, which for a wedding is one of the couple, using a private (not business) account on SIAE's Feste Private portal; a venue or wedding planner cannot buy it on that portal. A venue's own background-music subscription does not cover a private event. The penalty if checked without one is 30% of the licence amount. There is no fixed deadline, but it must be active before the event.
facts.source_name: SIAE (Società Italiana degli Autori ed Editori), 'SIAE matrimonio e feste private: la guida completa'
facts.use_note: Classic 'invisible work' item: ask the planner whether they will guide you through the SIAE licence and who is responsible. Note the couple holds the licence, even if the planner, band or DJ helps.

facts.claim: Noise from entertainment is regulated town by town in Italy under the national noise framework law (Law 447/1995) and each municipality's noise regulation. For example, the Comune di Verbania (Lake Maggiore) states that entertainment held inside buildings or on outdoor private property must respect noise limits, and temporary derogations are requested from the Mayor under its regulation.
facts.source_name: Città di Verbania, Autorizzazioni in deroga alle emissioni acustiche
facts.use_note: One example town only; do not generalise specific hours to all of Italy. Article angle: ask the planner what the music curfew is at your venue and who holds any permit. No national 'midnight curfew' should be stated.

facts.claim: The Reserve Bank of Australia rate on 22 October 2026 was 1 AUD = 0.6241 EUR (so EUR 1 is about AUD 1.60).
facts.source_name: Reserve Bank of Australia, Exchange Rates
facts.use_note: Conversion rate for every AUD approximation in this file. Over the three days shown it moved between 0.6217 and 0.6246, a reminder that EUR deposits cost a different AUD amount by the time they fall due. RBA notes its data should not be relied on for commercial purposes.

facts.claim: A 2025 report for Convention Bureau Italia and Italy for Weddings (research by Centro Studi Turistici di Firenze), presented with Italy's Minister of Tourism in February 2026, found about 16,700 weddings of foreign couples in Italy in 2025 (+9.8%), with turnover above EUR 1.1 billion. 46.8% of foreign couples used a professional wedding planner, symbolic ceremonies were the most common format (65.4%), and average spend per event was EUR 67,000. Tuscany led, followed by Lombardy, Campania, Piedmont and Sicily; the top areas were Lake Como, the Amalfi Coast and Chianti. The US was the largest market (31.7% of requests); Australia was named among growing long-haul markets.
facts.source_name: Ministero del Turismo (Italy), press release on the 2025 Destination Wedding in Italy report, Rome, 18 Feb 2026
facts.use_note: Best current market source; supersedes F-21 for figures. Strong lines: 'nearly half of foreign couples marrying in Italy use a professional planner' and 'Lake Como, the Amalfi Coast and Chianti are the most requested areas'. The 65.4% symbolic figure supports the legal section (many couples marry legally at home and hold a symbolic ceremony in Italy). Hosted on the Ministry site but the research is the Convention Bureau's, so phrase as 'a 2025 industry report presented with Italy's Ministry of Tourism'.

facts.claim: ISTAT recorded 3,378 marriages in Italy in 2024 between two foreign partners who were both non-resident, almost 2% of all marriages in Italy.
facts.source_name: ItaliaOggi, 'Matrimoni, spese alle stelle?' by Antonio Longo, 6 Jun 2026 (reporting ISTAT)
facts.use_note: Not a conflict with F-25 but a different measure: ISTAT counts legally registered marriages; the industry report counts all celebrations, most of them symbolic. Optional context for the legal H2: only a minority of foreign couples' Italian weddings are legal marriages registered in Italy. Do not present the two numbers as contradictory.

facts.claim: Federconsumatori figures (Italian consumer association, 2026) reported by ItaliaOggi: wedding planner fees in Italy run from about EUR 1,000 to EUR 3,500 for on-the-day coordination only, and from about EUR 2,500 up to EUR 10,000 to 15,000 or more for full organisation of more complex weddings or by the most established professionals. Many planners instead charge a percentage, averaging around 10% of the total wedding budget.
facts.source_name: ItaliaOggi (Antonio Longo, 6 Jun 2026), citing Osservatorio nazionale Federconsumatori
facts.use_note: Independent and dated, and already cited on our live /expert-advice/cost-of-wedding-planner page, so this piece stays consistent with it. Caveat for the writer: these are whole-of-Italy figures that include domestic weddings; a 70 to 110 guest multi-day destination wedding at Lake Como or Amalfi will usually sit at or above the top of the range. Say 'from' and 'or more', and link the cost page for detail. Conflict: our older page /how-to-plan-a-destination-wedding-in-italy-if-youre-overseas (2023) says 10% to 15% with no source; this source says about 10% on average and Vogue (F-28, US context) says 10% to 20%. Do NOT use '10% to 15%'. Say 'often around 10% of the budget, and higher for luxury studios' or give only the fee models. Prices go to Nic.

facts.claim: Vogue (Condé Nast) describes three ways planners charge: a flat fee (for a full-service planner in its US-focused example, about USD 5,000 to 75,000), a percentage of the total wedding budget (typically 10% to 20%), or a hybrid of a smaller percentage plus a flat fee.
facts.source_name: Vogue, 'What Does a Wedding Planner Actually Do?' by Shelby Wax (published Apr 2024, updated May 2025)
facts.use_note: Use for the fee MODELS (flat, percentage, hybrid), not for Italian amounts; the USD figures are US-centric and should not be quoted for Italy. Supports the brief's 'fee models explained plainly' gap.

facts.claim: A venue's own coordinator works for, and is paid by, the venue: Vogue quotes a destination planner saying the venue planner's 'allegiance is to the venue, not the couple', and notes that a coordinator typically works on a shorter timeline (often starting about a month out) and focuses on running the day rather than shaping the plan and hiring suppliers.
facts.source_name: Vogue, 'What Does a Wedding Planner Actually Do?' (updated May 2025)
facts.use_note: Supports 'where the venue coordinator stops' in H2 1. The quote is from a planner (commercial interest), so paraphrase as a general point and pair with our own cost page's line that a venue coordinator 'works for the venue, and scope varies from one venue to the next'. Do not name the quoted planner.

facts.claim: Foreign weddings in Italy are concentrated in May, June and July, but the season is lengthening: in 2024 October and November accounted for 22.4% of foreign couples' celebrations. In 2025 the last quarter of the year again grew its share.
facts.source_name: Quotidiano Nazionale (Antonio Petrucci, 17 Jul 2025), reporting the 2024 destination wedding observatory; 2025 trend from the Ministry release (F-25)
facts.use_note: Supports asking how many weddings a planner runs on the same peak weekend, and that shoulder-season dates are now common. Pairs with F-10 (May to September town-hall pressure).

facts.claim: Italy's standard VAT (IVA) rate is 22%, with reduced rates of 4%, 5% and 10% for specific goods and services.
facts.source_name: Agenzia delle Entrate, IVA: norme generali e aliquote
facts.use_note: Use as 'ask whether each quote includes Italian VAT (the standard rate is 22%)'. Do not state that every planner's fee carries 22% VAT: some small businesses use a flat-rate tax regime and VAT treatment of cross-border services can differ. Our live cost page already says planning attracts Italy's 22% VAT; keep wording as a question, not a rule.

facts.claim: Wedded Wonderland Concierge is 'a luxury wedding advisory and matchmaking service for modern couples'. 'Unlike a traditional wedding planner, we act as your trusted advisor and strategic partner during the sourcing and decision-making process. Depending on your wedding, we may recommend a partnered planner, or help you move forward confidently without one.'
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Concierge page (live)
facts.use_note: Brand fact (own page). Exact positioning for the final H2 and the honest 'not every wedding needs a full planner' line. Never call the Concierge a wedding planner. Tension on the same page: the 'Planner vs travel agent vs DIY' block says 'you need both, working as one'; follow the advisory wording above (see open_questions).

facts.claim: The concierge is a single point of contact for 'sourcing and securing the venue, negotiating with resorts and airlines, managing room blocks and guest travel, coordinating trusted local vendors, and handling deposits, payments and currency so nothing gets lost across borders.'
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Concierge page (live)
facts.use_note: Brand fact. Allowed in the contracts and currency H2 per the brief.

facts.claim: The concierge process has six steps: Discovery Call; Destination and Venue Strategy; Planning Assessment; Vendor Curation; Concierge Support; Travel and Honeymoon Concierge. A free Discovery Call is 'a complimentary, no-obligation call with a Wedding Concierge Advisor'. The enquiry form promises 'Reply in 24 hours', 'Fully confidential', 'No obligation'.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Concierge page (live)
facts.use_note: Brand fact. Live page shows '&' in step names ('Destination & Venue Strategy', 'Travel & Honeymoon Concierge'); brand profile writes 'and'. Either is accurate; follow the style guide. No prices: the page shows Concierge prices but the house rule bars them.

facts.claim: Proof points on the live concierge page: 800+ weddings and celebrations, 54 countries, 50k+ vetted vendors, 15 years of editorial authority.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Concierge page (live)
facts.use_note: Brand fact. Use one proof point at most. The page also shows '$1.2B in weddings and celebrations'; that figure is NOT in brand-profile.md, so do not use it. The Real Weddings quotes (Anya and Raoul at Lake Como, etc.) are not approved for reuse.

facts.claim: Our live cost guide states that a venue coordinator works for the venue and that scope varies from venue to venue, and advises asking in writing whether it covers suppliers from outside the venue, guest transport, the run sheet before the day, or anyone checking the band against the timings. It also advises asking every planner in writing: 'Do you receive any payment, discount or fee from suppliers you recommend, and do you mark up décor, production, entertainment or sound you supply?'
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, 'Cost of a Wedding Planner vs Planning It Yourself' (live)
facts.use_note: Own page, used for consistency and for framing the commissions question as standard practice (no allegation against any planner). This article should link to it rather than repeat its fee tables. Independent support for the commissions question: Brides '35 Questions to Ask Before Hiring a Wedding Planner' lists 'Do you receive any commissions or kickbacks from vendors?', but the page blocked our tools and was read only as a search snippet, so it is not cited.

facts.claim: Live vendor profiles confirmed on weddedwonderland.com on 23 Oct 2026: /vendor/italian-style-weddings (category 'Wedding & Event Planner', based in Lucca, Tuscany; profile FAQ says it plans across Italy including Tuscany, Lake Como, Rome, Sicily and Venice; languages English, French, Spanish, Italian) and /vendor/giritaly (category 'Wedding & Event Planner', Italy, listed under 'Similar vendors'). /vendor/dreamdust-weddings (planner, Turin) also appears.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland vendor profiles (live)
facts.use_note: Profiles exist, but naming them still needs planning-team sign-off (brief open question). Inconsistency on the Italian Style Weddings profile: stat block says '15+ years of experience' while the description says 'over 12 years'; do not quote either. Do not use the profile's weather or per-guest budget claims (vendor marketing). Giritaly profile itself not opened; confirmed only via the listing card link.

facts.claim: July 2026 was the hottest month recorded in Tuscany since observations began in 1955 (Consorzio LaMMA data). Around Florence, maximum temperatures exceeded 36 degrees C on 27 days across June and July 2026, with 27 'tropical nights' above 20 degrees C, and heatwaves are now far more frequent and longer than in the past.
facts.source_name: Agenzia Regionale di Sanità della Toscana (Tuscany regional health agency), 6 Aug 2026, reporting Consorzio LaMMA
facts.use_note: Supports asking for a heat plan (shade, timing of an outdoor ceremony, water, care for older guests) for a summer wedding in Tuscany. Do not generalise to all regions or promise conditions; no weather guarantees. One-year record, so frame as 'recent summers'.

legal.summary: Overseas marriages cannot be registered in Australia but are usually legally recognised if valid where they took place and valid under Australian law.
Recognition conditions: valid under local law and under Australian law.
Foreign certificate usually accepted as proof of marriage, may not prove a name change; check with BDM and a lawyer.
Nulla Osta required, preceded by an Atto Notorio with four witnesses from the Italian consulate for your state or an Italian tribunal.
Couple and four unrelated witnesses attend the consulate in person; each Australian partner signs their own Atto Notorio.
Atto Notorio valid six months; apostilled birth and single status certificates with NAATI Italian translations.
Nulla Osta sworn in person in Rome or Milan before an Australian consular officer; CNIs not valid in Italy.
No marriages at Australian embassies or consulates.
Civil ceremony steps at the town marriage office; Apostille on the Italian marriage certificate for use in Australia.
Peak season May to September can make town-hall and Apostille appointments hard to get.
SIAE music licence required for weddings away from home; the couple holds it.

needs.what: Italy-specific fee ranges for a 70 to 110 guest, multi-day destination wedding at Lake Como, Amalfi or Tuscany from partnered planners (flat fee and percentage, VAT treatment, what the fee excludes), with permission to publish as anonymised ranges. Independent sources only cover the whole Italian market (F-27).
Confirmation whether /vendor/italian-style-weddings and /vendor/giritaly may be named as partnered Italy planners in this article.
A real, consented example of how the concierge matched an Australian couple with an Italian planner (no names unless approved). Without it, the final H2 stays process-only.

Wedded Advisor confirmation of the current Italy legal process for Australians (Atto Notorio at the state consulate, Nulla Osta in Rome or Milan, Apostille on the certificate) and current consulate and embassy fees, as the Embassy page could not be loaded on 23 Oct 2026 and its PDF is undated.
Our own typical answer to 'how far ahead should we book a planner in Italy': no independent source found; planner profiles and blogs say 12 to 18 months, which is vendor marketing.
Concierge guidance on what the partnered-planner network is vetted for (registration, insurance, references), if the article is to say how the concierge checks planners.

Typical practice on professional indemnity or public liability insurance for Italian planners: no official source states it is mandatory for wedding planners, so the article can only suggest asking for it.

checks.note: All 38 facts carry source_url, source_type and checked (2026-10-23).
No fact rests on a competitor or aggregator. Matrimonio.com, planner blogs and planner directories were seen in searches and not used. Vendor profile (F-37) is our own site.

All legal facts from Smartraveller (Aug 2026), the Italian Consulate General Sydney, and the Australian Embassy Rome PDF (undated, medium confidence, flagged N-04). SIAE is the official collecting society.
8 price rows, all needs_nic_signoff true, EUR with AUD at RBA 22 Oct 2026 (0.6241). No Concierge prices.
The '10% to 15%' line on our 2023 page is not confirmed by an independent source (Federconsumatori via ItaliaOggi: about 10% average; Vogue, US: 10% to 20%). Writer told not to use it (F-27).
F-19 (UNI voluntary vs association 'sono legge'), F-26 vs F-25 (legal registrations vs all celebrations), F-27 (fee percentages), F-37 (vendor years).
